chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Joining Lionel Hampton's new band as drummer and singer
summary: Hampton formed his band with Sir Charles, Vernon Alley and Irving Ashby; Lee sang, beat Billy Eckstine in the Pittsburgh Courier poll, and left in early 1941.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: ended up being Sir Charles on piano, Vernon Alley on bass, and Irving Ashby, he came from Boston -- and Hamp was getting people from just not Los Angeles; musicians he had heard while he was with Benny, and Ray Perry -- he got Ashby and Ray Perry from Boston. Ray Perry played alto and violin, and trombone player ... real good one; his name starts with a B; but I can't remember his name.

And he had at this time -- he had ... did Ernie join us at first? I don't know if Ernie Royal went with us at first or not, but anyway, Hamp left here with a pretty good band. Every time we started leaving home, it looked like I wouldn't stay too long, you know, so ... because I didn't really like to rough it. We went up in the Northwest, and, you know, Hamp was quite successful - but I did all the singing with Hamp's band, you know.

Yeah, all the singing with his band, and it's a funny thing; that if you could see -- my son has a scrapbook -- the Pittsburgh Courier used to have contests, you know, male vocalists, drummer and trombone player. Well, the thing that I circled -- the year that I was in the contest, I was ahead of Phay Terrell and Billy Eckstein as a vocalist, so you know, in later years, after I quit fooling with singing and just started to play drums, I would look at that every once in awhile and think about, you know, if they ever thought
that I could get more votes, you know ...

Yeah, that was '40. That was '40, and probably '41, too, because the band got together in the summer, and I know we were in the Northwest about in October, because everyone had to sign up for the draft, you know, in October, and I think where I signed up was in Portland, Oregon, because we were on the road; that's why I remember that.
And so I stayed with them until early '41, but when he got ready to go to the Grand Terrace was when I left, and Shadow Wilson replaced me.
